brief: Institutional and systematic equity longs have been cut sharply. GS: US index positioning fell from a record 48% of open interest in May to 36%, CTA/systematic exposure from $145bn in August to ~$70bn after ~$75bn of selling, and GS's baseline sees CTAs buying ~$25bn next month. Despite that de-risking, hedge funds built their largest weekly Nasdaq short in over a decade, GS/CFTC data show $14.9bn sold and shorts up $15.8bn through September 22, even as Nasdaq hit fresh highs, while options traders keep chasing upside, NDX's 3rd-largest 1-month put-call skew decline on record. Nomura notes 2x realized vol on SPX up days versus down days, and stock dispersion at a 30-year 95th percentile is keeping index vol artificially low while AI/tech rips and Energy, Financials and Utilities lag. Underneath the S&P's highs, over 40% of Russell 3000 stocks have fallen 20%+ since June and the median stock is 16% below its 52-week high, breadth GS calls weakest since the Dot-Com Bubble. MS's Mike Wilson reads this as a mid-cycle valuation correction, not a fundamental break, given earnings-revisions breadth near cycle highs. GS flags light AI positioning despite the Meta Muse rally and likes renting upside in AI-commerce names.
